title: Migrate a blueprint toward Nix
description: Test a hybrid blueprint alongside an existing rcm setup and use coverage reports to decide which modules can move to Nix.

sections.title: Start with a working rcm blueprint
paragraphs: A hybrid setup is useful when some modules already have a Nix implementation and others still rely on shell scripts or package lists. Begin from a working blueprint, record the modules you expect to keep, and make the migration on a Git branch or a separate test checkout.

Install the Nix tooling required by your chosen adapter before testing the apply step. Home Manager manages user-level configuration, nix-darwin manages macOS system configuration, and the nixos adapter expects a NixOS host.

sections.title: Compare coverage before editing
paragraphs: Run the migration comparison for the blueprint profile you want to move. It classifies modules as ported, partial, blocked, or kept-rcm. Use the module-level results to choose a small first batch and note any modules that need a new implementation.
Keep a copy of the current report so you can compare it after changing manifests or module selections.

sections.title: Generate a separate starter configuration
paragraphs: Write the migration output to a fresh file in your test checkout. This creates a starter configuration so you can review it without overwriting your current smu.toml. Compare the files and carry over the existing profile module lists and any settings you still need.

The hybrid example uses Home Manager for supported modules and allows rcm fallback for the remaining modules. Merge that adapter selection into the reviewed blueprint configuration before preflighting it.
sections.code:
smu blueprint migrate --from rcm --to hybrid --output smu.hybrid.toml --json
git diff --no-index smu.toml smu.hybrid.toml

sections.title: Preflight the merged configuration
paragraphs: After merging the starter settings into your test checkout’s smu.toml, run the blueprint doctor and adapter preflight. Review the generated artifacts, required commands, unsupported modules, and fallback decisions. Run with SMU_HOME_DIR pointing at your test blueprint if your usual checkout is elsewhere.

If a module falls back to rcm, decide whether that is acceptable for the current migration phase. If it is blocked, check whether the required tooling is installed and whether module.toml publishes an implementation for the target adapter and platform.
sections.code:
SMU_HOME_DIR="$PWD" smu blueprint doctor --strict --json
SMU_HOME_DIR="$PWD" smu provisioning-adapter preflight --adapter hybrid --profile default --json

sections.title: Test one host before removing fallback
paragraphs: On your test host, apply the adapter and profile that passed preflight. The apply step prepares generated artifacts and runs the adapter operations. Check that the expected configuration appears and that a fresh shell, editor, or other affected application starts correctly. Keep the previous blueprint commit available and review rollback coverage before changing a primary machine.
Repeat the comparison as you port modules. Once each required module has an appropriate Nix implementation, test without rcm fallback and preflight again before switching additional machines.
sections.code: SMU_HOME_DIR="$PWD" smu provisioning-adapter apply --adapter hybrid --profile default
